title: Narrative
description: A signed walk through records that are already in the atlas: an ordered list of steps, each naming one event or one edge and saying in prose why this step follows. A narrative never changes what it walks — it is an argument beside the graph, not another edge in it — and it cites what it rests on beyond the records themselves. Several narratives may cross the same period and disagree; each is attributed and the reader compares them (CONTEXT.md).

sources.description: What the narrative rests on beyond the records it walks — the account being told is itself an argument, so it cites like an edge does (rule 6).

summary.description: What this narrative claims, in a paragraph: enough for a reader choosing between two accounts of the same period. Non-trivial by rule 20.

steps.description: The walk, in order. At least two steps, each with real text: rule 20, because the validator's keyword subset has no minItems.

ref.description: The record this step is about: an event id, or an edge id in its from--to--type shape. Nothing else — a narrative walks the graph and does not annotate sources or actors.

text.description: Why this step follows, in the narrator's own words. Non-trivial by rule 20.

window.description: Optional: the years to open on, so a narrative about 1961–1975 does not start on the whole span of the atlas. Historians' years, no year 0, from before to (rule 20).
